observation.visible_scene: An elevated/aerial view over a low-rise commercial-industrial area (a white multi-storey building on the left, a long red-trimmed warehouse in the centre-right, flat-roofed buildings in the foreground, roads and parking lots) beneath a dramatic dusk/dawn sky. A thin orange band lights the horizon behind silhouetted distant hills, while a thick grey cloud deck covers the upper sky. The sun is hidden behind the cloud layer but breaks through a horizontal gap on the right-of-centre, throwing a fan of crepuscular (god) rays downward over the city.
visible_changes: The bright sun-spot inside the cloud gap drifts gradually from the right side of the gap toward a more central/left position across the excerpt.
The fan of crepuscular rays changes orientation and intensity in step with that shift, becoming narrower and more vertically concentrated in the later frames.
The illuminated edges of the cloud gap subtly reshape, consistent with cloud material moving across the hidden sun.
Foreground buildings, roads and the horizon line keep constant positions relative to the frame edges, indicating the camera itself does not pan, tilt or zoom.
The overall scene brightness and colour cast remain essentially steady throughout the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the brightening is a sunrise or a sunset.
What drives the apparent leftward drift (cloud motion vs. parallax) and whether the sun-spot keeps moving after the crop ends.
Events before t=0 and after t=3.200 s.
uncertain_details: Possible tiny vehicles on the lower-left road are too small to confirm movement.
The exact magnitude of the sun-spot shift is small and could partly reflect changing cloud transparency rather than true positional motion.
Minor frame-to-frame flicker in ray brightness may be encoding noise.
